key_insight: OS-Helix trains a single computer-using agent to coordinate GUI actions and code execution end-to-end, rather than relying on prompt-level tool switching.
engineering_relevance: This enables more capable desktop automation for real applications where agents must both interact with interfaces and manipulate files, scripts, and system state.
method: Built a hybrid action space that unifies GUI commands and code execution in one policy.
Created verifiable training data via application-artifact composition and decoupled instruction/evaluator generation.
Improved the agent with online RL using Step-balanced GSPO to stop long code traces from dominating optimization.
evidence_signal: On OSWorld-Verified, OS-Helix-27B and 35B-A3B achieved 35.0% and 33.7% relative gains over hybrid baselines, and OS-Helix-27B-RL reached 66.44% success after a 42.9% improvement.
watch_item: The approach depends on high-quality hybrid supervision and live-environment RL, so data construction and action-step balancing may be costly and sensitive to implementation details.
paper_title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
